calm.title: The difference calm has made
calm.content:
I’ve been doing the daily meditations for a couple years. Occasionally, I miss a day, but I have developed a 15 minute routine where I sit outside in the early morning quiet, and listen to meditations with Tamara and Jeff and Jay. Sometimes I listen to just one, other times I have time for all three and every time I take something away. 

 I’ve noticed how I can hold onto Calm and steadiness throughout the rest of my day. I also have noticed when handling stressful situations lately, I tend to not react and get as overwhelmed, and I think this is the benefit of practicing daily centering meditations. I use the sleep stories and the sleep meditations, the daily meditations, and the soundscapes. And I recommend calm as often as I can!

calm.title: Would be a lot better with more intelligent features to reduce cognitive overload.
calm.content:
Been a Calm user for years. Recently saw an ad on Instagram that took me to quiz.calm.com. Had me answer a few dozen questions. I figured maybe Calm had a new feature to build a custom plan for me so I don’t just keep picking the same old meditations. Nope. It was just a marketing bait and switch. There’s not even a feature to build a plan based on the 25 questions it just asked me. Just wanted me to put in my credit card and subscribe (spoiler… I’m already a subscriber). Incredibly frustrating. 

So here’s the new feature you should build. Ask me those 25 questions from your quiz, but then build me a plan automatically based on it. When I open the app, I don’t want to have to go digging for the meditation I want. That could take minutes staring at a screen adding more cognitive overload to my life. Instead, create a plan for me and then allow me to tweak it over time. THAT would be valuable. THAT would keep me as a subscriber. I’ve found the app less and less useful over time and am probably going to unsubscribe, but that would help change it around for me.

calm.title: Finding Calm
calm.content:
I've had the app for a while as I got it through work. I didn't use it at all - I figured I knew enough about mindfulness and meditation. Then was hospitalized and  recovering from - new to me - severe neurological problems that were so bad I could no longer walk.
While in an excellent rehab hospital, one of the very first doctors that I saw asked if I was familiar with mindfulness and meditation. I said yes, but it's not something I've practicing lately. His first prescription for me was for me to return to practicing those things starting that evening, even if it was as little as five minutes. I remembered I had the Calm app and figured I should check it out as it was one of the tools he mentioned. It's been a lifesaver! I love it. I love the variety and I love all the daily check-ins. I've been using it daily for the last couple of months, and it's been so helpful - a life saver! Give it a chance - you may find a whole new set of tools ❤️

headspace.title: Headspace
headspace.content:
Based on my own experience of the Headspace app, I would give the product 4 out of 5 stars. My experience was largely positive, with specific strengths being ease of navigation, visual appeal, relevant and helpful material, accessibility options, and a wide range of content. This praise does not come without concerns, however, although some of the concerns may not directly come to mind as an adolescent. I worry about some of the privacy collection aspects of Headspace, although I am unsure how relevant this would be to the 13 year old looking for help with coping strategies. There are some concerns from an adolescent point of view, namely how little engagement there is in each activity. There are also limited opportunities for peer connection and a pretty hefty price tag starting in 2027.
Adolescence is a major point of change in a human’s life. Similarly to early childhood, there is a heightened point of brain plasticity that allows for the brain to change and adapt to new experiences. There was a time where individuals viewed this period of a child’s life as simply something that you just needed to get to the other side of. Laurence Steinberg challenges this idea and sees adolescence as an opportunity for children to truly develop certain skills. In his interview with Jonathan Singer on The Social Work Podcast, Steinberg (2018) states that this time is crucial for developing non-cognitive skills like mindfulness and mediation for self control. Headspace crucially allows space to develop these skills. If I am a student who is having trouble with transitioning to a new school or grade and looking for concrete ways to find relief, I have an app at my fingertips that will carefully guide me through exercises that teach me lasting coping skills. Lessons have colorful animations that engage me and durations that can be as short as 2 minutes if I am in a rush. 
In his book The Age of Opportunity, Steinberg also mentions how adolescence is beginning earlier and ending later. Steinberg (2014) states “a longer period between the start of adolescence (when the brain becomes more easily aroused) and when it ends (when brain systems that govern self-regulation have finally matured) means a longer period of imbalance, and greater exposure to all sorts of problems” (15). Headspace provides free plans for individuals as young as 13, meaning they can take advantage of this period of neuroplasticity to build healthy habits. This is a tool they could carry with them through this extended period of development, as the extensive library provides content all the way through later adolescence and into adulthood. The sooner children can find ways to cope with this greater exposure to problems, the better off they can be for future stages of development.
Adolescence is a time of increased autonomy. In Working with adolescents: A guide for practitioners, Laser & Nicotera (2021) note that “the youth moves from the external control of childhood moral behavior to autonomy and internal control in adolescence” (20). Adolescents increasingly want to have more control over their own lives and make their own decisions. Headspace gives them this opportunity to regulate their own behavior and emotions by allowing them to personalize their experience. They can open and use the app at their leisure and select which goals they want to work towards, which voices they want to hear, and how long they want to practice. An adult might recommend using the app, but this is an experience they get to maneuver on their own. Adolescents can eventually work towards independently recognizing when they need assistance and what they can do to help manage it. This is especially relevant because adolescence is the time where individuals experience more complex demands. Peer relationships become more important, identities begin to develop, there are increased academic demands, and family relationships may be changing as an adolescent works towards independence.
One large concern regarding Headspace comes from how adolescents view rewards. Laser & Nicotera (2021) explain that during adolescence, “the social-emotional brain, the limbic system, undergoes a change at about the time of puberty, 12–14 years old, which alters the youth’s attentiveness to rewards, sensation seeking, emotional arousal, short-term gratification, and adherence to social norms” (16). Headspace does not feed off of rewards in ways that might capture an adolescent’s attention directly. Of course, there is the reward of calming down from a stressful moment using one of the app’s exercises, but there is no instant sense of gratification for other parts of the app. There is a tracking feature that shows how many minutes and lessons have been experienced, and I believe that aspect could be expanded upon to increase engagement from adolescents. In the future, they may be able to include an awards page or allow for increased cosmetic profile customization as you progress through lessons.
Another drawback is how individual Headspace’s exercises are. Although you can share short segments of exercises with your friends, there is no way to directly connect with other individuals. Adolescence is a time where relationships and peer acceptance become increasingly important. These exercises can be helpful in some regards, as mindfulness can allow an adolescent to recognize when they feel socially overwhelmed and manage anxiety before entering a social situation, but there are no concrete ways to practice communication or develop relationships. Ultimately, these drawbacks are not significant enough to take away from the massive benefits this app provides for adolescents.

headspace.title: Ebb is impressive
headspace.content:
I’ve been someone who has struggled with anxiety my whole life, and the mix of meditation and therapy this app provides has been really effective for me. I have a three-pronged system in place. I speak to my therapist twice a week, meditate once a day, and externalize to Ebb during flare-ups of anxiety. These three things working together has made me feel a sense of progress I haven’t felt in a long time.

Ebb has especially come a long way since I first tried to use it when it was first introduced. It asks good questions, makes interesting connections from prior conversations, and can make effective suggestions to navigate specific moments. This will never replace my therapy, but to have a place to catch anxiety in the moment, talk through the lessons I’ve learned from my therapy, and work through things quickly with a cognitive behavioral approach, helps me catch anxiety before my day begins to spiral.

Very impressed and curious to see where things go from here.

headspace.title: 10-year review
headspace.content:
i’ve had headspace for over a decade. for the first 3-4 years, I loved it. this app’s approach toward meditation and wellness has noticeably shifted since its inception though. When I started, it was Andy Puddicombe doing all of the meditations, translating what he learned as a monk into meditations everyday people could use and understand. he made those meditations accessible. I appreciated and learned from his approach towards meditation and life. eventually, Eve, Kessonga, and Dora joined, bringing a new lens that i really enjoyed too. they were different, but it still felt like their approach overlapped with andy’s, and I felt they complemented each other very well. these teachers taught me so much.

andy left a few years ago. the app has shifted in the years since—and many may like the new version! I honestly don’t know. But a couple of the new meditation teachers (not all of the new ones) make meditations and wellness exercises that don’t feel like they are teaching me anything new. They often feel closer to generic wellness content from an instagram influencer than a guided meditation. Some of the lessons they teach directly conflict with the lessons of the earlier generation of teachers. I chose headspace originally to be taught a form of meditation environment I could only easily find here. I want new teachers to have spent years studying, practicing, and guiding clients through that form of meditation. I also want them to align with apps original approach. 

And I know this shouldn’t matter to me, but I find it grating that one of the new teachers uses their platform to sell supplements. 

Anyway, it makes me feel sad to see how the perspective of headspace has changed. it’s trying to be so much. why is it offering therapy now? and AI diary entries? i miss when it was simpler app with diverse perspective unified by a common approach. but I still use headspace, because all of the earlier content is still available, and I have more to learn from it. And so that is what keeps me coming back and paying. But only because I haven’t found a suitable alternative yet. And that’s disappointing because ideally, I’d like my subscription to include new content in the style of the original meditations. 

p.s. Also, the app suddenly doesn’t work with my VPN which is dumb. why does my meditation app need to know my ip address? please fix the vpn issue.

headspace.title: Fantastic Content, Terrible Navigation
headspace.content:
Hi, I love the content in this app. The meditations, the courses, the move workouts, the sleepcasts/music, it’s all great. Since the content is what’s most important, my rating is high. The content alone would be equivalent to a 5 star rating.

That being said, the app is SUCH a pain to navigate. I have to remember how to get to pages myself, because the “recommended for you” content on the front page is never related to what I’ve actually been doing in your app. 

There’s also no option to add in details of your life that might prevent you from receiving certain reccommended content. For example; I have no kids, and there are many meditations, ones that keep getting recommended to me, about being a parent. I should be able to mark an option to hide all of this content, or at the very least, tell the app to stop giving me it as a recommendation.

So in conclusion; content is fantastic. Actually got me to stick with a meditation and move schedule, and absolutely love it. PLEASE make the app itself work better on a functional level. I shouldn’t have to search “Walking” every day when I want to find a walking meditation.

Also give me an option to turn Ebb off. They aren’t helpful, and cause me more annoyance than anything because it literally cannot answer any question I ask it, and it simply just gives me the same 3 basic meditations as an answer every time.

If you leave the app while playing a track for too long or god forbid, open another app in the background, not only does the music stop, but the entire app resets and you cannot recall where you left off at all. The music and playlists never get updatedc and the selection is mid at best. Nothing memorable worth coming back to after you’ve listened once. The study beats library has stayed exactly the same over 2 years now with not a single new track. The layout makes very little sense and it’s not intuitive at all. Calm is a much better option than this. It doesn’t have to be this awful.

headspace.title: Learning to observe the mind
headspace.content: Headspace is my daily go-to. I’ve been using the app for years! Love Andy’s meditation wisdom insights as well as his sense of humor. I can honestly say its changed my life for the better.

headspace.title: Bad UX
headspace.content: I use this mainly when I can’t sleep. But the app is so cluttered and disorganized it’s so difficult to pick something I end up clicking all around at 2am & then I really can’t sleep.

headspace.title: Remove AI please
headspace.content: Used to love the content in this app, I don’t want AI pushed on me.

headspace.title: Great app, please fix recommended/recently played!
headspace.content: Headspace has played a massively helpful role in my life, however a few minor grievances have come up that have been consistently annoying in using the app. It seems like I always have to dig through my history to resume the last course I worked on, and it always has courses I have finished and haven’t touched for a long time front and center on the homepage. I would be very grateful for some major tweaks to how the app organizes its courses and recommends singles.

headspace.title: I miss the old headspace
headspace.content: I used to love using this app and used it for many years With the addition of an AI agent and a cluttered landing page, it’s clear that they want to increase engagement with the app at the expense of the experience. I just want calm and simplicity. Now it feels like every other app.

headspace.title: Lost its mojo trying to do more than it needs to
headspace.content: Poor execution on the app basics means I could care less about the new garbage they are trying to pitch. What is the purpose of this app anymore? It’s impossible to keyword search or filter sleepcasts. You can’t even read a description and see the voice until after you start it! Recent updates have killed my battery - there is no need to force the app open, just turn off my screen! I’m letting my annual subscription lapse and will be trying Calm instead.

headspace.title: Great… but leave out AI
headspace.content: This is a great app that has helped me a lot with anxiety. The one thing keeping it from a five star review is the use of AI. I understand what it’s trying to do, but I am concerned with the environmental impact caused by generative AI. I would love it if there was an option for reflection without the use of artificial intelligence.

headspace.title: It was a great meditation app
headspace.content:
Unfortunately, now the app buries its meditations in a back menu. It pushes lessons and therapies with pop-up screens and toasts. It has some AI thing built in that collects your personal information. It requests insurance information. It shows interstitial screens before and after meditations, prompting you for engagement. It tries to sell you therapy, and has no way to opt out, even if you already have a therapist.

It was a great meditation app. Now it's just a gamified, needy, upsell machine trying to feed every statistic it can learn about you into an algorithm.

No, thank you.

If you want to meditate, go for plum village instead.

headspace.title: Good but chaotic
headspace.content: Headspace is a solid app overall, and I really like the coaching feature. The guidance itself is helpful and easy to follow. However, the app layout makes it frustrating to continue guided programs. There’s no clear place to pick up where you left off and you end up guessing and clicking around to find the next session. The “Recents” section prominently shows classes I’ve already completed, which isn’t helpful. I don’t need front-and-center reminders of what I finished, show me what’s up next! Finding the next step shouldn’t be harder than doing the practice itself. The content is good, but the app is not laid out well.

headspace.title: paywall
headspace.content: everything is behind a paywall. useless

headspace.title: Half the app doesn’t function
headspace.content: I want to like it. The concept is nice, but most of the app is unusable. Nothing loads. I’ve follow the trouble shooting guide all the way up to uninstalling the app and reinstalling and it still just sits there. Until that’s fixed I don’t think I can give a higher rating. From what I understand this isn’t an isolated issue there are threads going back months on Reddit. I can’t recommend this until the issue is fixed, and suggest not wasting your money on a subscription on an app that doesn’t function correctly.

headspace.title: Slow, buggy
headspace.content: This used to be a great app, but it seems to be slowly degrading into a slow, bloated mess. Too many features, too hard to navigate, and basic features like opening up a meditation course where I left off now freezes/hiccups every time I try to use the app.

headspace.title: Impossible to get ahold of customer support
headspace.content: Ok for meditation. I booked a therapy session through the app because it accepts my health insurance, but there was no way for me to be able to make sure my insurance is linked to my account. I tried to cancel the appointment which is over the 48 hour period that they would charge you  a late cancellation fee and there is no way to directly cancel the appointment when you reach out to customer service It’s a bot telling you that someone will reach out to you in the next 48 hours which puts me in the window for the late cancellation fee. I’m really disappointed in the lack of customer service with this app. I won’t be renewing my subscription.

headspace.title: Completely locked behind a paywall
headspace.content:
Advertised as free but the only thing that’s free is singing up. They offer you a free trial, which I declined, and then could not do any of the exercises without paying. 

Why not just charge for the app if I have no choice but to pay? Greed is the only explanation.

headspace.title: Great content but app frequently glitches
headspace.content: I love the app when it works. I mostly use it for the sleep sounds. Often the app won’t load or will shut off randomly.

headspace.title: Discount code.
headspace.content: They have a discount code with planet fitness but no way to use it.

headspace.title: Has potential but money stealing
headspace.content: You have to pay for the one meditating thing, but I feel like it would be a good app. Definitely needs to let people not pay because this is just adding my stress.

headspace.title: Disappointed
headspace.content: The meditations have long silences that make me think my iPad has frozen if I haven’t nodded off. Unlike MyStrength, they don’t seem to have much wisdom to share.

headspace.title: Do not sign up for auto renewal.  Terrible customer service and policies.
headspace.content: I sent a cancellation request to Headspace via their app’s ai-powered chat support on the day my membership was to renew.  I got no response so I followed up 3 days later.  I was told that my annual membership fee of 99.00 could not be refunded because I was 3 days into it (at that point).  BUT, they would graciously turn off autopay since I no longer wanted to be a member!  I researched them online and heard many stories like mine.  Proceed with caution with Headspace.  There are many other apps and services with better customer service and policies that I would try before signing up with them.

headspace.title: Best Meditation App!!
headspace.content: I’ve been using head space since I was like 7 and I’ve continued to use it every night and throughout the day sometimes. It truly is so calming and relaxing and has been one of the only ways I can fall asleep at night. Pooch Palace was the meditation I listened to every night growing is and recently I have tried others and the name may have changed but it’s is the absolute best!!

headspace.title: subscription
headspace.content: literally unusable without paying for it. hell nah im going back to looking thru reddit for answers 🥀

headspace.title: 首页总是提示出错
headspace.content: 不知道其他人是否有这个问题，每次进入首页总是提示出错，需要退出后重新登陆才恢复正常。除此之外都是好的，是我每天都要用的App

headspace.title: Messy interface, patronizing content
headspace.content:
I get the paid version free from my health insurance. 

The basic meditation course is solid with present but minimal pretension.

Content is overall disorganized and I find it hard to find and refind items of relevance to me. 

Lots of soothing mental health "expert" voices, homogeneous and cookie cutter

I tried a sleep course, wanted to skip ahead to all the chapters to see if there's any value to it, but it's not letting me do it. Like a book that your can't skim to get an impression of.

Depressing to think that this is what passes for popular mental health.

headspace.title: Poor customer service for a mental health app
headspace.content: Headspace works with 3rd party companies to offer long term free trials with what seems to be the hope that you will forget about auto-renewal and get charged for a year subscription. Any other app would handle immediate requests for refunds appropriately, by offering a full refund or at the very least a partial refund. Instead Headspace adamantly denies refunds of any kind even when the request is sent THE SAME DAY of the charges. I signed up for a free 3mo trial, used it for about 3 days maybe, then forgot about it. Today I receive an email notifying me of the renewal charge of $79 and, given my current financial situation, freaked out because I just can’t afford that for an application I never use. Yes I should have cancelled, but life happens and you forget. But let’s not pretend this isn’t a ploy to hopefully collect money from a forgetful customer. It would be one thing if I used the app and even delayed requesting a refund til days or weeks AFTER the charge, with demonstrated usage after renewal… then I’d say yea, no refund should be given at all, because your product was being utilized. But that’s not my case, and $79 in THIS economy is a lot, and it’s absolutely disgusting that a mental health app makes no exceptions for instances like these when most mental health problems people suffer from HAVE EVERYTHING TO DO WITH FINANCIAL STRAIN! Do better, stop the greed, especially while selling us on caring about our mental health.

headspace.title: Doesn’t Function
headspace.content: This app doesn’t work. Most of the content won’t even load on a brand new iPhone 17 Pro. I contacted support and after trying everything they suggested (deleting the app, clearing the cache, restarting the phone, reinstalling the app, trying it on a different network, etc.)  they told me there was no timetable for fixing these issues and I should just use the web app. 🤣 Seriously? Why bother making a native iOS app then? I’d like to say the Headspace content is good at least, but having no convenient way to access it, I’m not sure.

headspace.title: Nothing free on the app
headspace.content: Not worth downloading unless you want to pay for it.

headspace.title: NO
headspace.content: This app is money hungry, I downloaded this app to see if it would be good in my free time because ive got an anxiety disorder it tries to make you pay while your signing in/logging in but if that doesn’t work it makes you pay to watch the tutorial video! SUCH STUPIDITY

headspace.title: Adorable.
headspace.content: Ah, yes its making my pay for everything I acctually need EXACTLY WHAT I WANT TO CALM DOWN       ✨🗣🔥

headspace.title: The only meditation app you need
headspace.content: I’ve been using this app for 8 years! I’ve tried other apps and always come back to this one. Andy’s voice is magical. How the meditation is set up puts me right into the zone and the voices of the meditation guides helps me keep focus. The app is also designed beautifully. From the characters, to the colors, the entire conceptual design is unique, interactive, and beautiful. I love the concepts, and they have so many different programs and collections to choose from. From different ways of helping you fall asleep, such as the soundscapes and sleep casts, to all of their meditation programs. I just love this app and all of the features it offers. The fact that it’s so well organized and easy to use makes it all the better.

headspace.title: App Issues and Deterioration
headspace.content: I have been a longtime user of Headspace. Unfortunately, recently it has been double counting sessions. The issue is that if you go to Daily Meditation and immediately change the duration it logs me as having completed two sessions instead of one and syncs that to Apple Health. I have been telling Headspace about this for months and they have said they would fix it, but have not done so. To make matters worse, I no longer get support responses from humans but rather from a bot. It seems to me that there has been general deterioration of the app and of support. I suspect that they are unable to manage their growth. I will be moving on to a different app.

headspace.title: Used to be great
headspace.content: I’ve used headspace off and on since their initial launch and always loved it, the platform and content were always fantastic. I just recently was planning to resubscribe. However, I was very disappointed to see the addition of an AI chatbot. I know every organization is tying to stay “current” with AI but it’s jarring. There is no question that use of AI is driving us to climate disaster faster (one of the anxieties I was hoping to temper with the redownload). I can’t continue to use a tool of it contributes to the exact thing I am looking for help with. Not to mention, unless the chat model is trained very, very carefully and monitored constantly, how can they prevent it from going off the rails. There’s already at least one documented case of a murder suicide due to an individual becoming too engrossed with an ai chatbot. That risk increases when the bot is given the additional credibility of a wellness platform. I’m sure this app is still for someone, but I’m very disappointed and it’s no longer for me.

headspace.title: Have loved this app for years but now it’s soured
headspace.content: I owe this app a debt of gratitude for being foundational to my meditation journey. I still love the instructors (especially Dora) but the app has been increasingly aggressive about pushing its Ebb AI thing at me, which is morally distressing and makes it difficult to focus on my meditations. I can theoretically ignore Ebb but not silence it, so I have to keep being reminded that I’m paying money to a company that is apparently more interested in “growth” than caring for the planet. Not exactly feeling centered, looking for more ethical meditation app suggestions.

headspace.title: AI slop
headspace.content: Why they ever thought it would be a good idea to start selling AI slop is being altered but… it’s gone from bad to worse.

headspace.title: Headspace chose greed
headspace.content: This was a great app but they’ve prioritized an AI robot for their management agent on the app and after a meditation it basically asks you to review the app and provide voluntary data for analytics. For a mindfulness app this seems pretty corporate and evil. AI is driving certain people to commit suicide on other platforms and headspace should be more mindful of their greed. Growth should not be more important than morality for these platforms.

headspace.title: The fact you have to pay is sickening.
headspace.content: They advertise for mental health but yet ofc it’s at a cost. Meanwhile most of us are f*kd up bc of our finances.

headspace.title: Give option to turn off AI
headspace.content: Otherwise its a great app

headspace.title: App crashes in courses and singles every time
headspace.content:
I like the content but what use is it to pay for the app if i cannot access the content because the app crashes every times in courses and singles which is the only thing that interests me. If I pay for a year and can’t access the content it makes me feel robbed.

I tried all the crash suggestions that they recommended of updating the OS, reinstalling the app, etc.

headspace.title: No more streak timer
headspace.content: Great app with many options. I use it to meditate daily and a few months ago, they took away the streak timer. It was something that kept me coming back as I’d always try to set a new record for the amount of days I meditated in a row.  My friend says insight timer has this and it’s free. I’m considering switching over after 5 years now

headspace.title: Great, except…
headspace.content: What happened to the watch app? Could you please bring back, it was incredibly helpful when unable to use the phone

headspace.title: They’ve made it too complicated
headspace.content: I’m now being forced to complete a quiz just to get into the app and meditate. I’m a paying subscriber. I didn’t want to spend time clicking on my phone completing an assessment. I just wanted to meditate. I’ve used headspace since 2018, but I think this will be my last year.

headspace.title: Best UI/UX of any app I’ve ever used
headspace.content: Best UI/UX of any app I’ve ever used

headspace.title: Missing a good wake up
headspace.content: I’ve used the app since 2020 and still rely on the daily meditations with Andy. I miss the wake up sessions that started my day. They’re often a meditation instead of a way to kickstart the morning.

headspace.title: Bring back the Today timeline! Terrible Customer Support!
headspace.content: I used to love this app and I’ve had the app for several years. I ended my subscription at the end of 2025. I renewed my subscription several days ago only to find out that today timeline discontinued. The new interface is not user-friendly at all. A meditation app shouldn’t take 10 to 15 minutes to try and every time. I am completely disappointed. A once beautiful app is no longer usable. Also terrible customer service! Can’t get a refund! Apple Store sends me to Headspace to Apple. It’s ridiculous!

headspace.title: Sold out
headspace.content: They decided to move the Ebb AI to where most people click for daily meditation, and now push Ebb and therapy. Shell of what it used to be.

headspace.title: Really disappointed
headspace.content: Nearly every feature costs money. Don’t even try to use a wind down or sleepcast. This app used to help me sleep a lot and it was really the only thing that worked :( it feels very deceiving to not make the app itself cost money and put these prices upfront. I don’t understand not being able to make at least one thing in each category as free, like the app used to be.

headspace.title: Quality has gone down
headspace.content: The sleep casts are nice but otherwise the app seems far too tailored towards affluent office workers living in a city. Its demographic is clearly one specific lifestyle. The app as a whole feels like it’s more investor run than anything these days. The AI implementation is terrible, I tried using it to start my day on a positive note and every morning it just tells me to call 911. I don’t see how calling the cops every morning would do anything other then maybe get my dog shot.

headspace.title: So much forced ai garbage
headspace.content: Constantly trying to get you to get therapy from a chat bot.

headspace.title: Headspace has changed my mind!
headspace.content: I subscribed to this app 3 years ago and it’s been the best tool i’ve found to practice meditation!

headspace.title: Horrible Customer Service + No More Lifetime Subscription
headspace.content:
I had previously contacted customer service to cancel my subscription, as I couldn’t do it through the website and had to do it via email request. It wasn’t cancelled, despite being told it was and not to worry, and I was charged anyway. I had to email multiple times explaining the situation s as to why the renewal wasn’t on purpose and I had been told it was cancelled previously to get a refund. It was worded as a “one-time courtesy,” they were “going to grant me,” despite that the renewal was a mistake on their end. 

Was planning on getting the lifetime subscription to Headspace for years because of how much it helped me with my focus and mental health, but they got rid of it, so I can no longer keep this app and use it like I planned and they said there are no plans to bring it back. I will be looking elsewhere now.

headspace.title: What a mess
headspace.content: All I want is to be able to press a widget and be able to launch the same set of guided meditations every single day. I am trying to build a practice, a foundation. Instead the app prioritizes nonstop discovery (I don’t care about the 100th niche meditation course) and buries my liked library of meditations

headspace.title: Why is a meditation app so chaotic?
headspace.content: I could never find a simple 10 meditation. It’s either a video, or a course, or a podcast, or something fancy. Even when I’m looking for a music, it’s kids music, story time, whatever course!!! I once loved meditation and so it so often, because of this app I actually stopped meditation because it’s always so overwhelming. What happens to less is more? Shouldn’t meditation be simple and straightforward?!?!

headspace.title: Love the quality of the meditations, hate how complex and and convoluted the app is now
headspace.content: Started meditating with this app years ago and it was life changing. Moved on to other platforms but came back recently.  Hate how complicated the new UI of the app is now, there’s too much going on.  App also keeps crashing when I try to browse the library of meditations, very frustrating.

headspace.title: Unethical and predatory subscription practices
headspace.content: Charged annual sub without notification. The service is of a very low utility, especially when there are plenty of AI options available today.

headspace.title: helpful and kind
headspace.content: This app has been one of my favorites for a few years. It has helped me on my meditation journey not only at the beginning but also now.  I have followed a number of the courses which are excellent,  repeated several of the courses which has help me grow, and today even reached out and got excellent technical help as I needed it.

headspace.title: getting worse
headspace.content:
i used to love this app. it must have been bought by private equity because it is so full of nonsense now. i no longer feel it's worth the price, so i have gone elsewhere.
it's a shame because their "sleepcasts" are unique and very effective. but it is offputting seeing they have sponsored ones now as well, i'm never going to listen to a star wars story to help me fall asleep or meditate and i don't like even looking at it. 

this is just like everything else now where profit is more important than quality. i don't need an AI to help me meditate or for my mental health. like really?? it stresses me out to even look at it.
it's like people have come in to add more "stuff" to make it /look/ like more value when all people want is quality over quantity. 
i'm truly bummed because i used to like this app a lot.

headspace.title: Sad
headspace.content: Sad to see the app is no longer accessible to everyone.  Is anything free? Why is the app free? You’re all con artists

headspace.title: Greedy developers
headspace.content: You now have to pay for everything on the app. So greedy…. It amazes me

headspace.title: Please fix ebb’s eyes
headspace.content: I’ve tried using Ebb and it’s not bad. But the design/character is really distracting. Every sentence or so, it keeps opening snd twitching one eye and it honestly bothers me. It really distracts the flow of the conversation I was having with it. Whoever decided it was a good feature to have… please fix it or have the option to keep the eyes shut and less disturbing.

headspace.title: Apple AirPlay incompatible
headspace.content: I really wish the sleepcasts had better compatibility. I’ve been unable to successfully get the sleepcasts to play on my HomePods especially when it comes to balancing the voice and the sound. It either only plays the voice or only the sound. Almost never both. With the new iOS update it doesn’t even play at all.

headspace.title: Major UI issues, can’t reach support
headspace.content: There are some glaring UI bugs and UX issues with the app. I can’t get in touch with anyone to report them because they’ve swapped out their entire customer support team with a dumb bot. There’s no option I can find to submit a bug fix request. I just keep getting bot responses.

headspace.title: It’s just breathing exercises
headspace.content: Headspace ultimately comes down to breathing — which is fine — but the way it’s wrapped feels counterproductive. Much of the content is more distracting than calming, with heavily scripted, almost performative skits that feel intentional rather than grounding. The app itself doesn’t help: the layout is cluttered, it’s not intuitive when you open it, and it doesn’t clearly remember where you left off. Instead of easing the mind, it often adds a subtle layer of anxiety.

headspace.title: Ruined this app
headspace.content: I’ve subscribed to Headspace for years and years. I just canceled my auto subscription yesterday. This is supposed to be a mindfulness app, but as soon as you open it you’re bombarded with pop-ups and try this! nonsense. They’ve ruined the UI completely, so that you can’t even access the course you’re on without going through multiple steps, yet the homepage is filled with tons of junk you don’t want. You cannot customize or change this, by design, so you keep getting pushed to features that will make them an extra buck. You cannot opt out of the AI/ therapy options, they will keep shoving them in your face, even if you aren’t interested at all. It’s so clunky, so hectic, and so stressful just to try to get to, again… a regular meditation. It used to be so elegant, and I would instantly feel calm and focused when I opened it. Now it puts me in a bad mood immediately. Sort these reviews by “newest” and you can see I’m not alone here. So many better apps at this point for meditation, this isn’t it.

headspace.title: App not working
headspace.content: I have been using headspace for years and within the last month it won’t let me advance on a course.  It just plays the same lesson over and over. The daily features won’t play. I pay for this service and it’s horrible. Not worth $75

headspace.title: Who Changed it?
headspace.content: I used to love headspace. I open the app and it had a list of the daily meditations I could achieve. Breath. Meditation. Explore. Night meditation release. Now I open the app and completely overwhelmed. Idk what to choose. So much is going on and nothing is going on all at the same time. I want the list back. Or at least the option for the list method.

headspace.title: App content great .. customer support sucks
headspace.content: The content of the app was great for a year but I was automatically renewed for a second year and I did not want it I quickly tried to cancel and they refused to give a refund.   The app while high quality was not valuable to me after the first year of use as I found other opportunities for meditation that were free.  I have asked nicely but they would not refund me b/c I cancelled two days late … no pro-rated refund nothing .. very very poor customer service and a complete corporate lack of empathy for customers … irony

headspace.title: Don’t buy on Apple!
headspace.content: You will be charged for Annual fee when you sign up for the Free trial, and they cannot help you with refund if you subscribed through Apple App. Yikes.

headspace.title: Total paywall
headspace.content: There isn’t a single function to try without paying, and it ain’t cheap.

headspace.title: Charged after cancellation
headspace.content: I canceled my subscription after receiving the email saying I would be charged soon. Despite canceling, my credit card was charged. I emailed customer service asking if I could be refunded since I had canceled and the charge was in error. Apparently the cancellation did not go through, and customer service told me I could not be refunded despite the representative acknowledging the possibility that the cancellation didn’t “take” on their end. Very disappointing customer service. Will not be subscribing again to Headspace.

headspace.title: App crashed, forgot streak
headspace.content: Over this holiday break I have been able to get back into a rhythm with meditation. I should be on day 9 right now but the app says my streak is 1. I think it happened because it crashed after my session yesterday and didn’t end the session the way it normally does (current streak, mindful minutes stats, a quote, etc.) I checked my stats in my profile yesterday and it was accurately report a streak of 8 so I don’t know where it thinks I missed a day but it does and that is really annoying.

headspace.title: Mindfulness??
headspace.content: I hate when app companies do this. I’m sure we’ve all been there. Headspace is the only app company that didn’t  refunded me when I notice a charge I hadn’t expected when its obviously i haven’t logged in in over a year. I purchased Headspace 2 yrs ago and used it twice. I thought I had canceled it. I saw the annual renewal charge email, still pending on my CC, & I immediately reached out to Headspace requesting stop payment or refund. I hadn’t opened the app in 18 months. They placated me with “we understand how frustrating this must be” in several emails up until I was denied; stating the cancellation period had ended. Cancelation period ended?? I  out minutes after I was charged. The charge was still pending on my CC. I shared all the screen shots with Headspace but no luck. I just think it’s good business practice to exercise rational understanding in such situations. I had chosen Headspace over the numerous meditation apps out there. I hope to eventually try mediation again, but it won’t be with Headspace. They could have easily won me over with a simple and expeditious solution, but Headspace chose a different path.

headspace.title: Addys review
headspace.content:
Do not get it unless
You want to pay for everything

headspace.title: Full of slop
headspace.content:
App is so full of slop it is becoming unusable. It is always trying to get me to try a new thing and always hitting me with pop-ups. 

It is difficult to pick up where I left off because I have to search for what I was doing before. The app isn’t interested in guiding me through a consistent course, it is rather always distracting me with some new thing.

It used to be better, this app gets worse and worse every year.

headspace.title: The good and the bad
headspace.content: The app, speakers, meditations, videos etc are all great.  The bad is that updates are not fully tested before being released.  They finally got the glitches from the last update fixed and then apparently ran another update and screwed up the stats.  I’ve been using the app since 2020 and have had my stats reset about 4 times due to updates.  I have only missed one day in 2021 and yet my run streak shows as 8 today.  It usually only takes a day or two to fix, but not this time.  The coders need to be more mindful.

headspace.title: best meditation app
headspace.content: Headspace not only helps you meditate it has guided programs for all kinds other things you might want to be working on like gratitude or managing stress, sleep health, etc. I have been using it daily since 2016 when I was dealing with the loss of my mother and my father’s grief of losing her also. It helps me manage the ups and downs of life.

headspace.title: Never ending charges
headspace.content: I canceled this service in 2019. But they just keep charging me. I contacted them and they referred me to Apple. I contacted Apple and they referred me back to these crooks. The subscription doesn’t show up on my Apple account anymore.

headspace.title: Recent Changes 👎👎👎
headspace.content: i used to love this app. the interface was great and it felt cozy. now it’s garbage. i wouldn’t be surprised to find out they fired everyone and have free chatgpt running the app because now images are pixelated, morning meditations have been repeating and today’s was even a BEDTIME one for kids! i really hate change but i might just go over to calm with the direction this app has been going in.

headspace.title: Disappointed
headspace.content: Confusing entry page, no clear navigation path, too much upselling, the Ebb AI feature is off putting, keeps crashing.

headspace.title: Amazing!

headspace.title: AI isn’t a substitute for Human Care
headspace.content:
AI isn’t and never will be a replacement, or even a valid form of support, for mental health, no matter how it is framed. This is particularly true of AI chatbots like Ebb. There is no compassion, understanding, or genuine identification with another human being. Think of a TV set used as a babysitter.

I’ve been a Headspace subscriber for nine years, which makes the recent changes especially difficult to watch. The meaningful 30-day courses are largely gone, aside from a few exceptions. The menus are confusing and cluttered, with too many offerings lost in a “more is more” approach that dilutes what once felt thoughtful and intentional.

The introduction of streaks and numerical tracking has also been counterproductive for me. Instead of creating a sense of accomplishment, it adds pressure and stress. Turning a wellness practice into something you “win” by maintaining a number feels fundamentally misaligned with the purpose of mindfulness, which should be about care and presence, not badges or scores.

I use AI all the time. I am literally using it now to help polish this text. I’m not a caveman. But I do not believe anyone should turn to an AI chatbot like Ebb to talk through something as profound as losing a spouse to cancer. We are human. Humans help each other. Humans care for each other.

I believe Headspace is losing sight of this in its push to become a more profitable endeavor. You are losing me a little more each day, and I genuinely grieve that.

headspace.title: Lost their way a bit
headspace.content:
I have used Headspace off and on for many years. I really like the meditation techniques and courses that are on offer. The decidedly “non-mystical” approach to various techniques is very approachable and I can say that Andy, through is app, has taught me how to meditate. 

That said, I find myself quite bothered by all the noise that has been added to the app in recent years. From a “check in” message that seems to show up after every meditation, to themed daily messages, “social” threads on meditations (thankfully you can toggle these off), and ads for their newer therapy services, I find myself wishing for a simpler version of the app that no longer exists. 

None of these little “noisy things” are inherently problematic, I just don’t have need for them or interest in using them. The compounding effect (to me) is an app that feels like it’s trying really hard to get me to “engage” with it in a “deeper” way, when all I really want is simplicity and meditation exercises that I can come back to.

I’m tired of seeing little “try this” or “check this out”-type messages in the app every time I use it. I don’t want ads for therapy services, I don’t want to talk to an AI chatbot about my feelings. I don’t care about “relevant seasonal content” that helps me “cope with the pressures of existential dread” or whatever. I want a meditation app with useful exercises and techniques. 

To be clear, those other things aren’t necessarily bad things, and others may disagree with me, but all this makes me feel like Headspace doesn’t have an identity anymore. It’s devolving into another “content” app that’s vaguely focused on mental health or something like that, and is really just trying to make the most broadly useable app for the largest possible audience, for the largest possible number of subscribers. Just my opinion though.

headspace.title: OG user SHOCKED at TERRIBLE updates. This is NO LONGER an app designed for mindfulness. Where’s Andy
headspace.content:
Original Headspace user here. Andy trained me in meditation one minute at a time until I was at 20 all the way back in 2015. At the start of Headspace, the app was like no other. I actually felt relaxed just opening it as it was so much clearer and more simple to navigate than all my other apps I find so exhausting. It was quick and easy to find my favorite sleep exercise and then my current course, and some meditations for special occasions or SOS. It was all I ever wanted or needed. 

I was so well trained I stopped needing the app after 5 years! But recently decided to return to brush up and WOW! This app has changed into something so chaotic, so illogical, so carelessly crafted, I see just about no evidence of relaxation or mindfulness in the design. It’s almost like now they’re attacking us with a fire hose of mindfulness content to sort through. 

Maybe we could get an alt version of the app? Maybe a better app will join the race. Sure hope so. 

Signed, 
Where is the spirit of Andy Puddicombe?

headspace.title: Cluttered w/clickbait + chaos
headspace.content:
I’ve used Headspace since 2015, so 10 years and counting. I used to love this app and referred it to so many people. I’m a paid lifetime subscriber. But it’s gone way downhill. The layout has become a complete mess and you get non-stop pop ups at every step of
The journey. Too many features and so much clutter in the app. For example, you used to be about 3 taps from a middle of night SOS session if you needed it. Needed a soothing meditation. Boom. There. Wanted to do a course instead of an individual. Boom there. 

Now it’s so featured packed and trying to do so many things it’s ironically a stressful experience. T try big to find your favorite l, go-to meditation? Good luck with that. 

Also, I say this as a lifelong Democrat and liberal: It’s also just overwhelmed with woke-ism. Desp it’s being quite liberal sometimes I’m overwhelmed by the world and actually don’t want politics, even my own politics, to be infused into what’s supposed to be a zen, calming experience. This is supposed to be a break from it all. 

And really loved it from 2015 to around 2019-2020. Then liked it from 2021-2022. But now, oof. I still use it occasionally but it is STRESSFUL to use. 

Please clean things up. Your job isn’t to drive app engagement. It’s to drive app consistency. There’s a difference. The former is about eating up the user’s time and taking advantage of their impulses. The latter is about giving them their time and life back. Please focus on this. 

Also, Andy’s voice was your competitive advantage. Why are you giving up on it? Other voices are a dime a dozen and any meditation app can replicate it.

headspace.title: No Refunds and Default Auto-Renewal
headspace.content:

I used Headspace on and off for a few months. The meditation served me alright, but it wasn’t something I needed to roll into a daily or even weekly routine. Somewhere along the year I thought I had cancelled my subscription. I received an email saying that my annual plan renewed. Since I hadn’t used the service for several months, I went back into the app to cancel. I was able to discontinue the automatic renewal (which I never manually turned on). I did this one calendar day after the auto-renewal. I couldn’t find a way to get a refund through the app. I went on their website and found out I do not qualify. So I’m out $70 USD because I was not aware of their buried setting. At least they sent an email confirming cancellation.

insighttimer.title: A decade of appreciation
insighttimer.content: I have been using this app for nearly 10 years and it truly brings tears to my eyes for how grateful I am of its presence. It has been a refuge and saving grace in my hardest times. There is so much I respect about this app. First and foremost, it has always been and continues to be accessible to anyone around the world. That simple core value speaks volumes in a world of paywalls. Anyone, at any time, can seek solace here without barriers. Second, you will always find an infinite amount of options for styles of meditation, lessons, music, etc. Any theme you may be looking for, it’ll be there. You’ll find teachers you love and come back to like an old friend time and again. And you’ll meet wonderful new ones anytime you’d like. Third and lastly, the timer was the core essence of this app long ago and still remains such a simple and perfect meditation tool. Even if you just use this, it’s a treasure. I highly recommend this beautiful and generous app for anyone at any stage in the meditation or healing journey - you’ll find a sacred home and community here, always ready to welcome you with such tender care. 🤍

Questions about why I stopped meditating, why I came back, what my goal is, am I ready to make a commitment, what time am i going to meditate every day, pages upon pages and absolutely no option to opt out. Then I got to the advertisements and that was another 5 pages. By the time I got to the home screen, I was so fed up with modern technology and capitalistic, constant-striving culture that I no longer felt like using the app anymore and I downloaded one that feels more aligned with what meditation is about.

Just Stop.

Absolute garbage.

insighttimer.title: Stop making me commit to streaks
insighttimer.content:
I’ve been using and loving Insight Timer for a long time. However, in the last year they have implemented some choices that have really not sat well with me. Primarily, it’s that they keep forcing me to ‘commit’ to streaks or how many days I’m going to meditate. This happens after sessions and sometimes when I load up the app. There’s no way to exit out of it - the app forces you to answer ‘how many days are you committing for?’ This isn’t cool. I’m not inviting or asking for the choice, and I either need to exit the app or make a choice on my commitment length that I don’t actually want to make and that’s not in integrity for me. 

It feels like they’re trying to force engagement and commitment. All they need to do is include a little X button to opt out of those screens. I don’t like feeling forced to put my word behind something that isn’t in integrity just to use the app.

insighttimer.title: It works with voiceover!
insighttimer.content:
I have advanced glaucoma and that means sensitivity delight, which means looking at a phone with its high intensity. Light is problematic.

I meditate every day and really enjoy meditation tapes to guide me through a specific focus point or just have some beautiful music.

The difficulty is when you can’t see the screen, how do you find the tapes and the teachers and continuing to meditate using apps?

I’ve gone through three or four of them, but none had voiceover assistance.

Voiceover is the ability to use iPhone and iPad and other Apple device devices without looking at the screen. You use a series of finger gestures.

For me that’s key because I listen to the meditation tapes at night and really don’t want to have to wake up. Focus on the screen to figure out where I am. With a couple of finger gestures, I can select the correct teacher and tape I want and is also a timing aspect so I can go to sleep listening to them.

Be aware, though it is not completely voiceover accessible. I keep running into dead ends and have reported it to tech-support as this is the best one we have and it can get better.

As to the tapes and the teachers in the music, nothing better I wish I had found this decades ago.

Truly wonderful collection of spirituality in one place

Disclaimer: I can’t see the screen so I dictate through Siri and that can cause unpredictable typos

insighttimer.title: WAS A must in this stage of my life.
insighttimer.content:
New review: I loved this app until it accidentally updated. I always intentionally avoid updates for various reasons, then wait until they work out inevitable bugs, but for all the newer features that are nice…there are a slew of issues that make this near useless for me. For instance… I built many playlists that I listen to often. I could stay in practice seamlessly, study for hours, fall asleep, whatever I chose. The screen would dim but the tracks would continue to play. Now, if the screen dims, or if I try to go dark to try and fall asleep, it illuminates after each track and stops so I have to hit play after every single track…what’s the point of wasting hours of time building playlists that don’t work and function like playlists???

The preview option is redundant and irritating and I see no way to turn it off. If I tapped a track before, it played 20-30 seconds of the track. That way I could tell if I liked the subject, voice, music, background, recording quality, etc. Now it goes to a different screen with a bunch of other tracks that have nothing in common with the one I want to just hear for a few seconds, and if I’m building a playlist it takes twice as long if I’m focusing on one teacher because I have to exit out of 2screens not just one and now it’s been over an hour of me trying to just meditate when I would’ve completed my nightly routine and been at calm, but it’s essentially useless. 

Who wants to snap out of meditation every 10-15, or even 30 minutes to hit play because now there are quadruple redundant steps to do what the old school system did flawlessly. I’m about to cancel my subscription, or..it could just be that instead of this being an easy lovely peaceful app like it has been the last few years for me, it’s turned into a nightmare. 

First review: Insight Timer has been incredibly helpful while going through difficulties, self reflection, or the little frustrations of everyday life. There are a vast variety of techniques, facilitators, subject matter, and other useful tools that are easily accessible, and for me, have proved to be invaluable. It didn’t take very long to figure out and find what I needed once I started using the app on a regular basis. It has become an integral part of my morning routine and I find myself going back to it more often throughout the day.

insighttimer.title: Starts at zero days practice every time it downloads an update!
insighttimer.content:

How can this be my first day using it when I’ve been using daily it for such a long time? Downloading an update for this application. Should not restart you at day one.

insighttimer.title: Love it
insighttimer.content: Has really helped with my meditation. Lots of great guided meditations and videos. Can’t recommend enough for someone just starting their meditation journey

insighttimer.title: Yoga sleep yah
insighttimer.content: I love this app, from morning wakeups to nighttime sleep tracks.

insighttimer.title: Bigger isn’t better
insighttimer.content: Still no way to mark the tracks or teachers I don’t like. Bigger isn’t better. Update: Did I just get a pop up about new live yoga right after I started my meditation timer? Yes. Yes, I did. Um, can’t the ads wait until after I’ve done my sitting practice? Updated review: some of the changes are good, but I think now that I've been using guided meditations more I've noticed places for improvement. First - it no longer switches to landscape view on the iPad - that's a small thing but it used to so now it's just frustrating. More importantly, to get to my bookmarked meditations, I have to go through something like 5 screens, many of them with very bright white backgrounds. In the dark morning this is very off putting. Finally, still, no download option means you have to be connected to the internet. I still love Insight Timer. The changes are great! One thing I would change: you can't rate a guided mediation unless you listen all the way thru. This means that 1)of course all the ratings are high bc who's going to sit thru 60 minutes of a bad mediation to rate it? and 2) there's no way to track those I've tried and didn't like. I wish there was some way to track negative ones as well as good ones. Older: This app has really helped me develop a meditation routine. Very dedicated customer service.

insighttimer.title: Excellent Timer
insighttimer.content:
The timer has some of the best recordings of meditation bells—which don’t cut off the sustain tail. 

However, the timer can’t be edited on Mac like it can on iPhone.

insighttimer.title: La mejor app
insighttimer.content: Excelente todo

insighttimer.title: Best Meditation App and much more
insighttimer.content: I use Insight Timer for inspiration, meditation, help with sleep, and to support psychological and physical health. So many wonderful teachers and features and always improving. For a small yearly investment you get access to all recordings, but you can totally find what you need with the free version.

insighttimer.title: Amazing
insighttimer.content: Easy to navigate, a lot of choices. I visit this site daily. It’s perfect

insighttimer.title: Lost its mission
insighttimer.content:
I’ve used Insight Timer for many years and have always appreciated what the app stood for: making meditation accessible to as many people as possible.

Unfortunately, over the last few years, it feels like the focus has shifted more toward monetization than accessibility. Features that were previously available with the free membership have gradually been removed or placed behind the paid subscription. I completely understand charging for premium content and features, but even some very basic sounds and options now require an upgrade.

What’s especially frustrating is the constant pop-ups encouraging you to upgrade while trying to use the free version. It makes the experience feel less peaceful and more like a sales funnel, which seems contrary to the purpose of a meditation app.

I don’t mind paying for a valuable service, but I wish Insight Timer would maintain a genuinely useful free experience while offering additional premium features for those who choose to upgrade. After being a longtime user, it’s disappointing to see the direction the app has taken.

insighttimer.title: Essential tool
insighttimer.content: I have been using insight timer since 2020. I found a great meditation that has been my medicine since ! Easy access and wow so many choices ! Absolutely LOVE IT. !

insighttimer.title: Thankful
insighttimer.content: The Teachers on Insight Timer are marvelous. It’s easy to find the teachers and meditations that resonate with you. Beautiful meditations

insighttimer.title: Distracting at times but generally great
insighttimer.content: I’ve used Insight Timer for many years at this point. It used to just be a timer, which is what I still use it for exclusively. Of course now there are all sorts of challenges that one is prompted to participate in, friends to meditate with and message, and other distractions. At least I find these distractions. Many people love them I’m sure. As for me, I always have to close out things I’m not interested in; I wish I could turn off being prompted in this way. But it’s still a great timer and now at least it defaults to the timer more than it used to; less things to close out. Anyway, it has great functionality as a timer, with interval bells and other things to keep one on track. Sometimes I use it for a short but inspiring 12 minute “Miracle Morning” SAVERS: Two minutes each of silence, affirmation, visualization, exercise (like jumping jacks), reading (from a deck of Virtues cards or other inspiration), and scribing/writing. Presently my minimum meditation is six minutes of the first three and I find it very helpful and clarifying. Thanks, Insight Timer!

insighttimer.title: Easy, well-considered app
insighttimer.content: I have found this app to be a very easy introduction to meditation. It has a variety of options to let a person try different types and lengths of meditation. It can be easily picked up and something found any time of day to suit your needs. I love the playlist option. I really appreciate that it is free.

The book basically instructs White men how it is their duty to continue with racism and called people of color “half devils.” The sleep story was not a book, but another short story of his. I brought it to the team’s attention, but they concluded that they wont remove the short story. The app is culturally insensitive. As an educated woman of color, I cannot support an app that supports the works of a racist author.

insighttimer.title: Love this app!

insighttimer.content:

I keep using it because the meditation brings me peace in a chaotic world.

insighttimer.title: LOVE it - Only One Issue
insighttimer.content:
I’ve recommended this app to hundreds of patients over the years and use it all the time myself. The ONLY reason I consider trying/recommending an alternative is that I don’t see a way to change the “streaks“ display from consecutive days, to # of days of meditation that week..  regardless of the goal it made you set. So they finish a meditation, feel great & proud of themself.. and instead of celebrating 5 days of meditation that wk, it’s like “ope sorry, you missed yesterday so we’re gonna show you a 1 instead of a 5.” 

Seems small but it takes away from that feeling and for a lot of folks... it’s enough to break their habit and confidence or shift the mindset. I preach to patients that perfection isn’t the goal so this is counterintuitive, but I value the tracking, goal setting, and accountability to goals set for themselves. 

Maybe it’s not technically a streak if it’s not consecutive days but maybe, given the purpose of meditation and this app, there’s another name for it or strategy or ability to set it for days in a given week.. so people feel good and maintain momentum 🤷🏻‍♀️ Just a thought. Otherwise I absolutely love it and try to prioritize using it every day myself.

insighttimer.title: The best meditation yoga, journaling, happiness inducing, mental health, soothing sounds/music app

insighttimer.title: Insight Timer has become an essential part of my daily meditation practice.

insighttimer.title: Has gone downhill
insighttimer.content: This used to be a wonderful resource that I used very frequently but I am disappointed by its introduction of videos. We don’t need a meditation app that has videos, we needed yall to just continue offering reputable audio. And some of the videos I’ve seen are so weird and have nothing to do with meditation or aligned with the integrity of the practice- such as advice for aging women and GLP1s and a 2 hour talk on the history of England. I get that yall are trying to create an open space for creators, but let them head over to YouTube and keep them a quiet space for certified meditation  practitioners to guide others. insighttimer.title: Please let us skip the opening prompts
insighttimer.content: I’ve been a paid insight timer user since 2021 and I have shouted it room the rooftops as the best meditation app/timer out there most of that time.  It’s been immensely valuable, so thank you! For the past year or so, however, I dread opening the app if I’ve set it down for more than a few days because of the gauntlet of goal/intention setting prompts that you apparently can’t fully opt out of. I shouldn’t have to “recommit to my practice” if I haven’t opened the app in two weeks. I understand that you want to incentivize people to use it through gamification but if it doesn’t change I’m going to cancel my annual subscription and move on to a simpler, less prescriptive option. And I just spent five minutes writing this review rather than meditating as I intended. Bummed.🫤

insighttimer.title: Incredibly valuable, and free

insighttimer.title: Wonderful
